description:
defstruct takes a default per field, but only a literal term: a number, atom, string, boolean, nil, or a list, tuple or map of those. A default that computes or names something is refused with the diagnostic parse/struct-default at the default:

    defmodule Tally do
      defstruct [:name, count: Enum.count([1]), seen: MapSet.new()]
    end

Elixir accepts any expression, evaluates it once when the module is defined, in the defining module (its aliases and imports), and every %Tally{} that omits the field starts from that value. That is the oracle.

Cause of the restriction: a default is carried on StructDef as a LiteralTerm and lowered where the struct literal stands, as the expression that writes it (Lowerer::lower_omitted_struct_field). A call or an alias lowered there would resolve in the using module, not the defining one. A literal names nothing, so it reads the same everywhere.

Done when: a default that is a call, an alias or any other expression is resolved in the defining module and gives Elixir's value on interp, run and build against oracle fixtures; fixture 00860 (the refusal) and the parse/struct-default code go, or stay only for what Elixir also refuses; LiteralTerm goes if the general carrier replaces it. Proposal page first: the choice is between evaluating at definition and carrying a value, or carrying the expression with its defining scope. Does not block fz-sc8.19 or fz-3ul.4: every default they need is a literal.
title: A defstruct default is any expression, evaluated in the defining module
